name: How the Fire Is Laid
description: A Woodfolk forester's instructions for laying the fire, cut into a slat of oak and tied to the lean-to's ridge-pole with bast.

name: Rubbings from the Lodge
description: A sheaf of charcoal rubbings of the mason's marks on the lodge's door-jamb, left folded in a crack of the jamb by a Sayers' student who ran out of paper.

name: What the Clansman Heard
description: A clan drover's account of what he heard at the stone, scratched on a scrap of hide and pinned to the stone's bow-knot with a thorn.

name: The Torch Count
description: A count of torches taken and given, knotted into a cord tied to the basket's handle, the knots stiff with pitch.

name: A Reel of Knotted Silk
description: A gatherer's reel wound with pale weaver silk already spun into thread, knotted at every hand's length in a pattern of three and five.

name: A Forester's Evening
description: A forester's notes of clan fires counted from the bench, written on the white inside of a strip of birch bark and tucked under the cairn's top stone.

name: An Oroth Mason's Wedge
description: An iron wedge of Oroth make, black and unrusted, found lying in the moss at the foot of the block that moved, its striking face bright as if it had been hammered last night.

name: The Planters' Round
description: A planters' list of notches answered, cut into a hazel stick with a sapling's name beside each notch, tied to the trench's marker post.

name: The Tender's List
description: A moss-tender's list of the mosses on the bed and the dead they are for, written in oak-gall ink on a board kept under the bark roof.

name: The Vigil Roll
description: A Hart-Knight's roll of vigils kept, lettered on vellum and rolled into a hollow antler tine hung by a thong from the tent-pole.

name: The Brother's Strides
description: A woodfolk child's measure of the Fourth Brother's strides, a line of hazel pegs driven into the verge behind the stone, the newest three pale and fresh-cut.

name: A Count of Fires
description: A count of fires seen to the east, chalked on the flat stones round the cold hearth in a small, careful hand.

name: A Keeper's Mark-Stick
description: A Rookhold keeper's mark-stick for the Briar root, notched for each visit and carved at its head with the Old Gate's sign, driven into the ground by the mouth.

name: The Lamp-Runner's Card
description: A lamp-runner's card of dusks, a square of bark with a knot burned into it for every evening the lamp was lit from the Hearth, hung inside the shrine's hood.

name: What Was Not Said
description: A folded sheet of bark-paper wedged between two of the stones, the unsaid half of a Fernhold argument written out in full and never delivered.

name: The Smith's Order Book
description: An antler-smith's order book, the leather cover scorched, left open on the forge's cold hearth-stone with a pair of tongs laid across it.

name: A Relic-Dealer's Prices
description: A price list in a Tollmere dealer's hand, the paper greasy and folded into eighths, dropped by the pegged hides.

name: Wenna's Wish
description: A Vale woman's last wishes, written on good Tamwick paper and kept in a clay jar sealed with wax, set on the ledge of the house's one standing gable.

name: The Carriers' Tally
description: An oil-carriers' tally, a notched yoke-peg for every jar carried to the Moot, kept on a thong round the stone's waist.

name: The Verderer's Count
description: The verderer's autumn count of harts, written small on a strip of deerskin and tied round the stone's neck below the carved head.

name: A Carter's Cup
description: A horn cup on a leather thong, hung from the tallest of the leaning stones for tipping the stones their share, the horn stained dark with cider.

name: A Carter's Question
description: A Tamwick carter's question, chalked on a slate and propped against the untaken loaf, the chalk already blurred by a week of dew.

name: A Letter from Tamwick
description: A letter from the family who built the lodge, left in a tin under the hearth-stone for whoever of the Wold would read it.

name: The Pickers' Weights
description: A pickers' tally of trays dried and weighed, scratched on a flat stone by the scales, lit faintly green where fungus dust has worked into the scratches.

name: The Rafters' Flood Roll
description: The rafters' roll of floods marked on the stone, lettered on a strip of oiled canvas and wrapped round the stone below the lowest mark.

name: The Round-Book
description: Hazelwick's round-book of stools and their turns, bound between two hazel boards and left on a stack of hurdles by the fire.

name: The Locker Tally
description: A tally of poles and ropes in the locker, cut into the alder root at the mouth, with a line of fresh cuts at the end that no rafter owns to.

name: The Watch Kept
description: A wall-watcher's night notes, written on a strip of bark with a burnt stick and left in the lean-to, the last lines trailing off the edge.

name: A Note Left in the Middle
description: A note folded under a stone in the exact middle of the bench's seat, in a sawyer's big square capitals.

name: A Snarer's Tally
description: A snarer's tally of wire set and taken, scratched on the inside of a strip of bark and left on the coiling-stump.

name: A Child's Dare
description: A list of the Hollow's children who touched the silk in the doorway, cut into a hazel stick pushed into the ground outside it.

name: A Guild Licence
description: A Tallymen's licence to strip bark in the Wold, sealed and stamped and nailed to a stripped oak, with a woodfolk bow-knot drawn over the seal in charcoal.

name: The Knight's Questions
description: The questions the Hart-Knight asks at the stones, lettered on vellum and tied to the tallest stone with a strip of hart-hide.

name: The Knocking-Words
description: A strip of birch bark with the Woodfolk words for knocking on the ring, tied round a low branch with green thread and a knot of moss.

name: The Verderer's Roll
description: A roll of the road's keepers, written in green ink on a strip of deer-hide wound round the staff below the hook and tied off with the horn's cord.

name: The Stump's News
description: A copy of the rumours on the broken waystone's stump, written out in a careful hand on a leaf of bark and wedged into a crack in the stone.

name: The Burner's Leave
description: A verderers' leave to burn fallen wood, sealed with green wax and nailed inside the hut's door, the wax cracked and the nail new.
